body:
## Summary
The clip publish gate's rule of who may do what in which state is written three times: as a doc comment in the contract, as refusals in shadowrunr-clips, and as a line-for-line TypeScript copy in the console. Move the rule into shadowrunr-types as one pure function, `ClipCandidate::act_block(ClipAct) -> Option<ClipActBlock>`. The store, rerender and publish code call it to refuse. The daemon derives a read-only `acts` field on every candidate it returns, and the console renders that field instead of re-deciding.

## Description
This is a contract that two sides re-implement. ipc-contract / generated-type-contracts (one-authority-per-vocabulary) says the engine authors and the interface receives machinery output. The clip states already cross as a generated enum. The transition rule over them does not cross, so approveBlock, canRender, canPublish and the reject guard in the console are hand mirrors of store.rs, scan.rs and upload.rs. The day the daemon adds a refusal (for example a new gate state), the console offers a button the daemon refuses. The reverse also happens: the console hides one the daemon would allow.

The new types:
- `ClipAct` = {render, approve, reject, publish}.
- `ClipActBlock` = tagged {status{status}, no_render, needs_reauthoring, held_by{checks}}.
- `ClipActs` = per-act `{blocked?, override_needed?}`.

`ClipStatus::as_str` replaces status_name. Refusal prose in the daemon's errors is rendered from the block, so the console text and the daemon error share their cause. The console keeps only the wording. The leaning technique is ipc-contract / generated-type-contracts, section 'Generate the bindings between vocabularies', applied here to the state-to-allowed-act binding.

## Flow
- Add ClipAct, ClipActBlock and ClipActs, plus `impl ClipCandidate { fn act_block, fn acts }`, to crates/shadowrunr-types/src/clips.rs, with a 5x4 table unit test
- Add `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] acts: Option<ClipActs>` on ClipCandidate. ClipStore::load fills it and ClipStore::save strips it
- store.rs approve/reject, scan.rs rerender and upload.rs publish_dry_run refuse through act_block. status_name is deleted
- Regenerate packages/contract
- clipModel.ts drops approveBlock, canPublish and canRender. ClipActions.tsx reads c.acts and keeps the wording table keyed by ClipActBlock kind

## Expected impact
The four owner acts that the console and the daemon now decide separately get one decision site. A new refusal lands in one Rust function and reaches the console at the next generate with no TS edit. The console can no longer offer a disabled or enabled button that disagrees with the daemon. The 5x4 table becomes the gate's executable spec.

## Evaluation
Claim: the clip owner-act rule has one authority, and the console renders it.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no ClipAct type, no `acts` on the wire, console rules are hand copies)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first (Rust table test in shadowrunr-types, store/scan/upload refusal parity in shadowrunr-clips tests, console dom test on `acts`)
Result: better
Gate: architecture (the shared contract changes, but only additively: a derived read-only field)

title: Check-id vocabularies cross the contract as enums, not documented strings

body:
## Summary
Two gate vocabularies cross the wire as String with their members listed in doc comments: the sandbox session checks (10 ids) and the clip publish-gate checks (10 ids). Producers in three crates spell them as free literals, and the console hand-copies one list into `Record<string, string>`. Make them `SandboxCheckId` and `GateCheckId` enums with the same serde names. SANDBOX_CHECKS becomes `SandboxCheckId::ALL`, and SANDBOX_WATCHED_CHECKS becomes `is_watched()`. The contract then generates literal unions, and the compiler checks every producer and the console's label table.

## Description
The vocabulary is closed but encoded as an open one. A typo in a producer such as "stage-ack" makes a new check that never gates and that the console labels through human(). A renamed check leaves the console's CHECK_NAME stale with no signal. This is ipc-contract / casing-and-naming ('call names are a vocabulary, not strings') together with generated-type-contracts ('the generator describes the wire'). The schema says string while the wire carries one of 10 values, so the TS type tells the consumer less than the contract knows. The change does not alter the wire: serde names are identical, so stored reports and candidates still parse and nothing is irreversible. The sandbox check set is the gate a recorded session passes. Typing it closes the gap where a producer reports a check the gate does not know.

## Flow
- Add SandboxCheckId (10 variants, ALL, as_str, is_watched) and GateCheckId (10 variants) to the types crate
- Change SandboxCheck.id and GateCheck.id to the enums. check_gates and gate_pass take the enum
- Producers in daemon sandbox.rs and record/watch.rs, cli.rs, sim sandbox.rs and clips gate.rs pass variants instead of literals
- Regenerate the contract
- Type the console's CHECK_NAME as Record<SandboxCheckId,string> and the gate-check labels as Record<GateCheckId,string>

## Expected impact
Two 10-member vocabularies get a single authority each. Mis-spelled or unlisted check ids become compile errors in Rust and TS instead of silent extra rows. The console's label tables become exhaustive by construction. About 30 literal sites go away.

## Evaluation
Claim: the sandbox and clip gate check ids cross the contract as closed enums with one authority.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no SandboxCheckId or GateCheckId, schema id is string, CHECK_NAME is Record<string,string>)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first (serde round-trip and ALL-order tests in shadowrunr-types, a report re-serialization test, the schema $ref assertion in schema.rs tests, a console typecheck with a seeded missing key)
Result: better
Gate: architecture (the shared contract changes, with byte-identical wire values)
